long_biography.plain_text:
The family apparel enterprise began as Ronald de Waal's grandfather's menswear wholesaler and became a substantial Dutch chain under his father. Ronald entered in 1977 and almost immediately pushed beyond the Netherlands, starting with a Swiss acquisition. When he succeeded his father in 1984, HIJ already had a broad domestic base but remained centred on men's clothing.

De Waal widened that platform by acquiring Witteveen and converting its women's shops into ZIJ. The two formats eventually converged as WE Fashion, supporting further European expansion and a broader portfolio that came to include O'Neill and Van Gils. WE now combines physical stores with a broad international digital-distribution network. Professional executives handle daily operations, while de Waal remains the controlling family owner.

Official company registers identify Belgium as de Waal's country of residence and give Wijnegem or nearby Antwerp-area addresses. The dossier proposes only the supported country field and does not infer a secondary residence from business, yacht or racing activity.

Forbes-first exact-name and company searches found no dedicated Ronald de Waal profile. No identity-secure personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Wikipedia article or personal website was found. A similarly named Amsterdam coach at ronalddewaal.nl is a different person and was excluded; WE Fashion's website is institutional rather than a personal profile.

Apparel retail is assigned because de Waal's wealth, control and defining operating mandate all satisfy its approved semantic contract. Published acquisition or build dates vary from the authoritative relationship start dates, so the vessels are used only for identity resolution and excluded from the biographies.

Both biographies exclude vessels, racing, wealth estimates, private-company values, transient store totals, annual financial results and source-language narration. The long biography uses only a general cross-border description to explain the durable international scope of the operating platform.
